phonics.title: The Bun
phonics.text: Meg has a bun. A pup ran up to Meg. The pup got the bun and ran off. Meg is mad.

questions.question: What did the pup do?
questions.answer: Got the bun and ran off.

phonics.reason: 'sat at Meg' is a wrong preposition and 'sat' does not lead to stealing; now the pup ran up to Meg.

phonics.title: The Bus
phonics.text: Ben and Nan got on a bus. Ben had a nap. Nan did not nap. Nan pats Ben. Ben is up. Ben and Nan get off.

questions.question: Who got on the bus with Ben?
Why did Nan pat Ben?
questions.answer: To get him up (so they could get off the bus).

phonics.reason: 'had to get Ben up to get off' is an odd verb phrase; simpler wake-up sequence.

phonics.title: The Hen
phonics.text: Nan has a hen. The hen ran off. It ran in the mud. Nan ran and got it. Nan got it in a pen.

questions.question: What did the hen run in?
Where did Nan put the hen?
Why did Nan run?
questions.answer: To get the hen (it had run off).

phonics.reason: 'ran off in the mud' was muddled; split into two clear sentences; 'got the hen in a pen' now 'put it in a pen'.

phonics.title: Bob in Bed
phonics.text: Bob is in bed. The sun is up. Dad is in. Dad pats Bob and Bob is up. Bob had a hug.

questions.question: Why did Bob get up?
questions.answer: The sun was up (and Dad woke him).

phonics.reason: 'Dad ran in' / 'got Bob up' and unexplained 'not mad' removed; kept wake-up idea.

phonics.title: Tim in the Sun
phonics.text: Tim has a rug. Tim sat on it in the sun. Tim got hot. Tim ran to a hut. Tim is not hot.

questions.question: Where did Tim sit?
questions.answer: On a rug in the sun.

questions.question: Why did Tim run to the hut?
questions.answer: He was hot / to get out of the sun.

phonics.reason: 'It got hot' was ambiguous (the rug?); 'ran in a hut' now 'ran to a hut'.

phonics.title: Chip the Dog
phonics.text: Josh has a dog. It is Chip. Chip ran in the mud and got wet. Josh got Chip in the bath. Chip sat in the bath. Josh got wet as well.

questions.question: Why did Josh put Chip in the bath?

phonics.reason: Josh appeared from nowhere; now he owns Chip.

phonics.title: The Jog
phonics.text: Quin and Mum jog on the path. The sun is hot. Quin has no hat. Mum has a big hat and a cap. Mum got the cap on Quin.

questions.question: Where do Quin and Mum jog?
Why did Mum get the cap on Quin?
questions.answer: The sun is hot / Quin had no hat.

phonics.reason: 'got it on Quin' odd and 'it' had no clear referent; Mum now has a spare cap.

phonics.title: Vin in Bed
phonics.text: Vin is in bed. He is hot and red. Dad got a wet rag. Vin is not as hot. Vin is not sad.

questions.question: What did Dad get for Vin?

phonics.reason: Rag 'on his chin' was odd; now put on Vin, and he cools down.

phonics.title: Zeb the Cat
phonics.text: Zeb is a cat. Zeb hid in the bin and had a nap. Jen shut the lid. Zeb is in the bin! Zeb is sad.

questions.question: Where did Zeb have a nap?
Why is Zeb sad?
questions.answer: He is shut in the bin.

phonics.reason: Story gap: why would Jen shut the lid on a cat; now she did not see him.

phonics.title: The Moon
phonics.text: Jess and Dad sat in the car. It was night and the moon was high. Jess had a nap. Dad had to keep on going.

questions.question: Who sat in the car with Dad?
Why did Jess have a nap?

phonics.reason: 'why' had no clue; added tired. 'had to keep on going' reworded.

phonics.title: Rain
phonics.text: It was raining. Ben had a big coat on. Sam had no coat and got wet. Ben let Sam get in the coat with him. Then Sam was not wet.

questions.question: Why did Ben let Sam get in his coat?
questions.answer: Sam was wet / he had no coat.

phonics.reason: Two in one coat needed to be plausible: big coat.

phonics.title: The Goat
phonics.text: Mark has a goat and a hen. The goat got in the barn and had the food for the hen. The hen is sad. Mark got the goat off. Then the hen had the food.
phonics.reason: 'the hen food' -> 'the hen's food'; 'got the goat off' -> 'out'.

phonics.title: The Torch
phonics.text: It was dark. Tim had a torch but it had no light. Tim sat on a log. Mum ran to Tim with a big torch. Mum had a hug for Tim.

questions.question: Why did Mum run to Tim with a big torch?
questions.answer: It was dark and Tim's torch had no light.

phonics.reason: Boy sitting on a road in the dark was unsafe/odd and 'light on the car' confusing.

phonics.title: The Chair
phonics.text: Kim sat on a chair in the park. It had jam on it! Kim got up and the jam was on her top and in her hair. Kim was sad.

questions.question: Where did Kim sit?
questions.answer: On a chair in the park.

questions.question: Why was Kim sad?
questions.answer: She had jam on her top and in her hair.

phonics.reason: 'her top had jam on it' clumsy; tense fixed.

phonics.title: The Chick
phonics.text: The farmer had a hen and a chick. The chick ran off. The hen was sad. The farmer had to look for the chick. It was in the barn. The farmer got the chick back.

questions.question: Who had a hen and a chick?

phonics.title: The Shower
phonics.text: Josh is in the shower. He got soap in his hair. The soap fell on the mat. The mat is wet now. Dad got a mop.

questions.question: Why did Dad get a mop?

phonics.reason: Sequence made no sense (soap fell, then mat 'wet now'); tense unified.

phonics.title: The Bus
phonics.text: Josh and Nan went on a bus. The bus had men and kids on it. Nan sat down. Josh had to stand. A man got up and let Josh sit. Josh said thanks.

questions.question: Who was on the bus with Josh and Nan?
Why did the man get up?
questions.answer: Josh had to stand / had no seat.

phonics.reason: 'why' had no clue: now Josh has no seat.

phonics.title: The Crab
phonics.text: Pam and Jim went to a rock pool. They had a look at a crab. Jim bent down to pick it up. The crab pinched his hand! Jim yelped and jumped back.

questions.question: Where did Pam and Jim go?

phonics.title: The Flag
phonics.text: Stan and Jess got a flag at the shop. They ran up the hill and stuck it in a crack in a rock. A strong wind hit the flag and it fell down.

questions.question: What did Stan and Jess get at the shop?
Where did they stick the flag?
questions.answer: In a crack in a rock on the hill.

questions.question: Why did the flag fall down?

phonics.reason: crack in a hill is odd; 'wind hit the flag' reworded.

report: Patterns: wrong prepositions and odd verbs (sat at Meg, got Ben up, ran in a hut, got the thorn/goat off), story-logic gaps (why Jen shuts the lid, soap/mat/mop order, a torch-less boy on a road, no seat on the bus, a 'who is Josh' with no link to Chip), vague 'it' referents, and unnatural phrases (pat a crab, the hen food). Tense clashes fixed only where the phase allowed. Left alone: P1-0, P2-1, P2-5, P3-4, P3-5, P4-0, P4-2, P4-4, P5-0, P5-1, P5-5 (read acceptably, or the natural fix was not decodable at that phase, e.g. 'her chin', 'were', 'out').
